title: Mediterranean Beef Stew
ingredients: 500 g (1.1 lb) of lean beef stewing/braising steak (in steaks, not diced)
600 g (1.3 lb) of green olives, stones removed
1 large clove of garlic, finely chopped
steps: In a large saucepan or casserole dish, gently fry the onion and garlic in plenty of good olive oil for a few minutes, taking care not to brown them.
Season the beef well with salt and black pepper and immediately add to the pan. Fry until evenly sealed and lightly browned.
Add the olives and tomatoes to the pan and simmer gently for two hours with the lid on.

title: Menudo (Mexican Tripe and Hominy Soup)
ingredients: 2 tbsp red pepper flakes (with the seeds)
steps: Wipe the dried Anchos off with a wet paper towel.
If desired, toast dried chilies on each side 15 seconds on a hot griddle (this releases essential oils and enhances the flavor).
Place the dried chilies into the small pot of boiling water and boil for 10 minutes, turning frequently in the boiling water to ensure all sides receive their fair share of punishment.
Remove the chili pot from the stove and drain off the boiling water. Fill with cold water; let it sit a few minutes to cool.
Remove the stems from the chilies, cut chilies longitudinally from stem to tip on one side and open. Flush gently with running cold water to remove the seeds.
Place stemless and seedless reconstituted chilies into a blender and purée.
Remove pure from the blender and place in the refrigerator overnight.
Rinse and drain the white hominy.
Place the patas (feet) and ribs into a pot.
Place the hominy in the pot with the patas (feet).
Put 1 tbsp salt in the pot.
Take 3–4 dried Chilis de Arbol, discard the seeds and stems, and snip the chilis into ringlets and put into the pot.
Cover with water to a height not exceeding 1 cm above the ingredients and bring to a boil.
Cook the posole uncovered until the ribs are finished. Remove from the heat.
Remove the meat from the ribs and dice into small cubes, place back into the pot with the posole, discard the bones.
Place the cooked patas (feet) into the pressure pot you will use to make the menudo.
Place a small pot of water on the stove and set to boil. This will be needed to prepare the chilies.
Cut the fat from off of the tripe. If fat clings to the non-honeycombed side of the tripe, use a stiff brush to remove it.
Cut tripe into small pieces, about ¾–1 inch. Strong scissors work well here!
If the tripe smells overly rank (this is normal), you may want to soak it in clean water for an hour (or possibly boil it in water for five minutes) throwing away the soak (boiling) water.
Place cut tripe into the pressure cooker on top of the patas (feet).
Add the garlic, bay leaves, and Mexican oregano.
Fill pressure cooker with water until about 1 cm. above the height of the stew ingredients.
Cook at pressure 35–40 minutes.
After the stew has cooked in the pressure cooker at full pressure for 35–40 minutes, remove from the heat and let the pot cool off completely until pressure returns to ambient.
Remove the patas from the pot and remove the bones. Put deboned patas into pot with the tripe and discard the bones.
Transfer the stew to a large bowl and add the posole, ensure all savory pieces lie below the waterline, and set in the refrigerator overnight.
In the morning, skim all hardened fat from the surface of the stew which has probably gelatinized overnight.
Reheat a serving portion of the stew in the microwave or on stovetop. When hot, place into a serving bowl.
Add a tablespoon of chili to the stew and blend thoroughly.

The menudo is ready to serve with hot corn tortillas. The spices (oregano and chili flakes) are traditionally combined before serving and placed at the side of the bowl of menudo with a lime wedge for the diner to add just prior to eating. Along with the spices, diced onion or cilantro are also traditionally added to the stew just prior to enjoying.

title: Mesir Wat (Spicy Ethiopian Lentil Stew)
ingredients: ½ teaspoon salt, or to taste
Fresh parsley or cilantro, chopped, for garnish
steps: Place the rinsed red lentils in a large pot and add the water. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer the lentils for about 15–20 minutes or until they are soft and cooked through. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking. Once cooked, remove from heat and set aside.
In a separate large pot, heat the olive oil over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion to the pot and sauté until it becomes translucent and slightly browned.
Add the minced garlic to the pot and sauté for an additional minute until fragrant.
Stir in the berbere spice blend, tomato paste, ground cumin, ground turmeric, salt, and black pepper. Mix well to combine the spices with the onions and garlic.
Add the cooked lentils to the pot, including any remaining cooking liquid. Stir well to incorporate the lentils with the spices.
Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook for an additional 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, to allow the flavors to meld together.
Taste the stew and adjust the seasoning with salt and pepper if needed.
Remove the pot from the heat and let rest for a few minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or cilantro. Enjoy hot with injera or bread.

title: Minestra
steps: Combine the courgettes, aubergines, pumpkin, onion, and kohlrabi in a large pot or pressure cooker. Add the vegetable stock and 1 tablespoon of olive oil. Bring to pressure and cook for 8–10 minutes, or simmer for 1 hour. Cool, then purée the whole thing.
Place a large handful of basil leaves and about 6 cloves of garlic in a mortar and pound until roughly crushed and a gritty paste is achieved. Add to the pot, stir and season to taste.
Meanwhile, boil the beans separately until soft, then add to purée mixture.
Boil the pasta until al dente then add to mixture.
Serve with grated Parmesan or hard Edam sprinkled over it.

title: Moqueca de Peixe (Brazilian Seafood Stew)
ingredients: 1 kg fresh white fish, cut into two finger-wide strips/slices
2 mid-sized onions, cut into circular slices
2 bell peppers (one red, one green), cut into circular slices
4 ripe tomatoes, optionally skinned then chopped
4 cilantro stems with leaves, finely chopped
12 tablespoons Azeite de dendê (a very tasty, heavy, saffron-colored palm oil, which may not be omitted under any circumstances)
steps: Leave the fish in a marinade made out of lemon juice and fine powdered pepper for at least 1 hour.
Put the fish, onions, bell peppers, garlic, tomatoes and the cilantro in numerous layers into a pot.

Pour the azeite de dendê and the coconut milk over all, and boil everything for 20 minutes. From time to time, ladle/scoop the liquid from the pot's bottom to its top. Be careful, in order to not break the fish!
Season to taste with salt.
Serve with white rice.

title: Yetsom Shiro (Ethiopian Vegan Chickpea Stew)
ingredients: 1 cup chickpea flour (also known as besan or gram flour)
¼ teaspoon cayenne pepper, or to taste
Fresh cilantro or parsley, chopped, for garnish
steps: In a dry medium-sized saucepan, toast the chickpea flour over medium heat for a few minutes until it becomes fragrant and lightly browned. Remove from heat and set aside.
Heat the olive oil in the same saucepan over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and minced garlic, and sauté until the onion becomes translucent.
Stir in the berbere spice blend, paprika, turmeric, cumin, cayenne pepper, and salt. Mix well to coat the onions and garlic with the spices.
Add the toasted chickpea flour to the saucepan and stir to combine it with the spice mixture.
Gradually add the vegetable broth or water to the saucepan, stirring continuously to prevent lumps from forming.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer the stew for about 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chickpea flour is fully cooked and the stew has thickened to your desired consistency.
Taste and adjust the seasoning with salt or additional spices if desired.
Remove from heat and let the stew rest for a few minutes to allow the flavors to meld together.
Garnish with freshly chopped cilantro or parsley. Serve hot as a main course, accompanied by injera or rice.

title: Zambian Beef Stew
ingredients: 1 pound beef, cut into bite-sized pieces
steps: In a large pot, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat.
Add the finely chopped onion and minced garlic to the pot. Sauté until the onions are soft and translucent.
Add the bite-sized beef pieces to the pot and brown them on all sides.
Pour in the beef broth or water and bring the mixture to a simmer.
Add the diced carrot, potato, tomato, green bell pepper, and red bell pepper to the pot. Stir well to combine with the other ingredients.
Season the stew with paprika, cayenne pepper, ground cumin, ground coriander, and salt to taste. Adjust the seasoning according to your preference.
Let the stew simmer for about 1–1.5 hours or until the beef is tender and fully cooked. Stir occasionally during cooking to prevent sticking and to ensure even cooking of the beef and vegetables.
Remove the pot from the heat and let the stew rest for a few minutes before serving.

title: Zambian Fish Stew
ingredients: 1 pound fish (e.g. tilapia, catfish, or any firm white fish), cut into pieces
steps: In a large pot, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and minced garlic to the pot. Sauté until the onions are soft and translucent.
Add the diced tomato, green bell pepper, and red bell pepper to the pot. Cook until the vegetables are tender.
Pour in the fish stock or water and bring the mixture to a simmer.
Gently place the fish pieces into the pot, making sure they are submerged in the liquid.
Season the stew with ground cayenne pepper, ground paprika, ground cumin, ground coriander, and salt. Stir well to distribute the spices.
Cover the pot and let the stew simmer for about 15–20 minutes, or until the fish is cooked through and flakes easily with a fork.
Taste the stew and adjust the seasoning if needed, adding more salt or spices according to your preference.
Remove the pot from the heat and let rest for a few minutes before serving.

title: Smothered Chicken Thighs
steps: Pat thighs dry. Season with salt, pepper, and paprika.
Brown in oil, 5 minutes a side. Set aside.
Cook onion in the drippings, add garlic. Stir in flour 1 minute.
Whisk in broth and milk. Return thighs. Cover and simmer 25 minutes until tender.

title: Weeknight Lemon Garlic Chicken Breasts
steps: Pound breasts even. Season.
Sear in oil 4 minutes a side. Add garlic 30 seconds.
Add lemon juice and broth. Simmer 5 minutes until cooked through.

title: Chicken Tortilla Soup
steps: Simmer chicken in broth 15 minutes. Shred.
Sauté onion and garlic. Add tomatoes, beans, spices, broth, and chicken.
Simmer 10 minutes. Serve with crushed chips.

title: Weeknight Beef Chili
steps: Brown beef with onion. Drain extra fat.
Add garlic, tomatoes, beans, and spices.
Simmer 25 minutes, stirring now and then.

title: Skillet Lasagna
steps: Brown beef with onion and garlic.
Stir in marinara, water, and broken pasta. Cover and simmer 18 minutes.
Dot with ricotta, cover with mozzarella, lid off heat 5 minutes.

title: Pork Chops with Skillet Apples
steps: Season chops. Brown in oil 4 minutes a side. Set aside.
Add apples, butter, cinnamon, and broth. Cook 5 minutes.
Return chops to the pan 3 minutes.

title: One-Pot Chicken and Sausage Jambalaya
steps: Brown sausage, then chicken. Set aside.
Cook onion, pepper, celery, garlic. Stir in rice 1 minute.
Add broth, tomatoes, seasoning, meat. Cover and simmer 22 minutes.

title: Shrimp Creole
steps: Cook rice.
Sauté onion, pepper, celery, garlic in oil.
Add tomatoes and seasoning. Simmer 15 minutes. Stir in shrimp 5 minutes until pink.

title: Ground Beef Tacos
steps: Brown beef with onion. Stir in spices.
Warm tortillas.
Fill with beef, tomato, lettuce, and cheese.

title: Chicken Fajitas
steps: Slice chicken, peppers, and onion. Toss chicken with spices.
Sear chicken in oil, then peppers and onion.
Serve in tortillas with lime.

title: Spaghetti and Meatballs
steps: Mix beef, egg, breadcrumbs, salt. Roll 16 meatballs.
Brown in oil. Add garlic and marinara. Simmer 15 minutes.
Boil spaghetti. Serve with sauce and parmesan.

title: Italian Sausage and Peppers
steps: Brown sausage. Slice if links.
Add peppers, onion, garlic.
Stir in tomatoes and seasoning. Simmer 15 minutes.

title: Oven-Fried Catfish
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Oil a sheet pan.
Mix cornmeal and spices. Press onto fish.
Bake 18–20 minutes until flaky.

title: Sheet-Pan Salmon and Broccoli
steps: Heat oven to 425°F.
Toss broccoli with oil and salt. Roast 10 minutes.
Add salmon, lemon, pepper. Roast 12 minutes more.

title: Venison Chili
steps: Brown venison in oil with onion.
Add garlic, tomatoes, beans, spices.
Simmer 40 minutes. Works with trimmings or mystery grind.

title: Pan-Seared Venison Backstrap
steps: Bring meat to room temp. Season well.
Sear in hot oil 2–3 minutes a side for medium-rare.
Rest 8 minutes. Slice across the grain. Butter on the slices.

title: Slow Venison Shoulder Pot Roast
steps: Heat oven to 300°F. Brown roast in oil.
Add onion, tomato paste, broth. Cover.
Bake 2 1/2 hours. Add carrots and potatoes last 45 minutes.

title: Mystery Meat Tomato Skillet
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb unlabeled game or beef cubes
steps: Cook rice.
Brown meat cubes well. Add onion and pepper.
Add tomatoes and spices. Simmer 20 minutes until tender.

title: Oven BBQ Chicken Thighs
steps: Heat oven to 400°F. Season thighs.
Bake 25 minutes. Brush with sauce.
Bake 15 minutes more until sticky and cooked through.

title: Red Beans and Rice
ingredients: 1 lb dried red beans or 3 cans
steps: If dried, soak beans overnight or quick-soak.
Brown sausage. Add vegetables.
Add beans, broth, seasoning. Simmer 40 minutes. Serve over rice.

title: Egg Fried Rice
steps: Scramble eggs in oil. Set aside.
Fry rice and peas. Add soy.
Fold in eggs and green onions.

title: Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry
steps: Slice steak thin. Mix soy and sugar.
Sear beef, set aside. Stir-fry broccoli and garlic.
Return beef with sauce 1 minute. Serve over rice.

title: Chickpea Coconut Curry
steps: Cook rice. Sauté onion and garlic.
Add curry powder, tomatoes, coconut milk, chickpeas, salt.
Simmer 15 minutes.

title: Greek Sheet-Pan Chicken
steps: Heat oven to 425°F.
Toss chicken and potatoes with oil, lemon, oregano, salt, garlic.
Roast 35 minutes.

title: Simple Lamb Stew
steps: Brown lamb in oil.
Add onion, broth, thyme, salt. Simmer 50 minutes.
Add carrots and potatoes. Cook 25 minutes more.

title: Chicken in White Wine Pan Sauce
steps: Season and brown chicken in butter. Set aside.
Cook shallot. Deglaze with wine, add broth and thyme.
Return chicken 8 minutes.

title: Black Bean Tacos
steps: Sauté onion. Add beans and spices. Mash lightly.
Warm tortillas. Fill with beans, avocado, lime.

title: Sausage and White Bean Soup
steps: Brown sausage with onion.
Add garlic, beans, broth. Simmer 15 minutes.
Stir in spinach 2 minutes.

title: Crispy Pork Shoulder Tacos
steps: Heat oven to 300°F. Rub pork with spices.
Add onion, garlic, orange juice. Cover and roast 3 hours.
Shred, broil 5 minutes for crisp edges. Serve in tortillas.

title: Ground Turkey Taco Skillet
steps: Brown turkey with onion.
Add beans, corn, chili powder, salt.
Top with cheese, lid 2 minutes.

title: Ham and Pinto Beans
steps: Cover beans and ham with water. Bring to a boil.
Add onion and garlic. Simmer 1 1/2 hours until creamy.
Salt at the end.

title: Crispy Duck Breast
steps: Score skin. Season.
Start skin-side down in a cold pan. Render 10–12 minutes.
Flip 3 minutes. Rest 8 minutes. Slice.

title: Salt-and-Pepper Roast Chicken
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Pat chicken dry.
Rub with oil, salt, pepper. Stuff lemon and onion.
Roast 70 minutes to 165°F in the thigh. Rest 15 minutes.

title: Sunday Beef Stew
steps: Brown beef in oil in batches.
Add onion, tomato paste, broth, thyme, salt. Simmer 1 1/2 hours.
Add carrots and potatoes 35 minutes more.

title: Garlic Shrimp over Pasta
steps: Boil pasta.
Sauté garlic in butter and oil. Add shrimp 3 minutes.
Toss with pasta, lemon, salt.

title: Pantry Tuna Pasta
steps: Boil pasta.
Sauté garlic in oil. Add tomatoes, oregano, salt.
Fold in tuna and pasta.

title: Sausage and Cabbage Skillet
steps: Brown sausage.
Add onion, cabbage, apples, salt.
Cover 12 minutes until tender.

title: Oven Jerk Chicken
steps: Mix spices, sugar, oil, garlic. Rub on chicken. Rest 20 minutes if you can.
Bake at 400°F 40 minutes.

title: Shakshuka
steps: Sauté onion, pepper, garlic. Add tomatoes and spices. Simmer 10 minutes.
Make wells, crack in eggs. Cover 6–8 minutes until whites set.

title: Wild Hog Chili
steps: Brown hog with onion. Drain if very fatty.
Add garlic, tomatoes, beans, spices.
Simmer 45 minutes. Good for trimmings and mystery grind.

title: Skillet Dove with Peppers
steps: Cook bacon, set aside.
Sear dove in bacon fat 2 minutes a side.
Add onion and jalapeño 3 minutes. Crumble bacon over.

title: Squirrel and Potato Stew
steps: Brown squirrel in oil.
Add onion, broth, salt, pepper. Simmer 50 minutes.
Add potatoes and carrots 25 minutes more.

title: Leftover Meat Hash
steps: Dice potatoes and onion. Fry in oil until brown.
Add chopped leftover meat and salt.
Fry eggs on top if you want.
